newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sells dlrs at 867.00 to support won.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sells dlrs at 867.00 to support won.

text.p: South Korea's central bank intervened in mid-morning trading on Monday, selling dollars at 867.00 won to limit the local currency's fall, dealers said.
"The rising trade deficit is largely to blame for the won's fall," said a dometic bank dealer.
On Saturday, South Korea posted a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billiion for January, compared with $2.13 billion a year earlier.
"Demand for the dollar is steadily rising because of sluggish exports and rising imports," the dealer said.
The won remained at 867.00 after the Bank of Korea's intervention. It had risen after opening at 864.50.
